options.text: No — the input $0$ is paired with both $5$ and $8$.
No — the output $3$ appears for two different inputs.
options.why: A shared output for different inputs is allowed; it does not break the function rule.

options.text: Yes — every $y$-value in the table is different.
options.why: The $y$-values are not all different, and in any case that is not the test — repeated inputs are.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly completes the definition? "A relation is a function when ..."

options.text: ... each input is paired with exactly one output.
... each output is paired with exactly one input.
options.why: This describes a one-to-one relation; a function only restricts inputs, not outputs.

options.text: ... every input and every output value is different.
options.why: Outputs may repeat across inputs; only an input with two outputs is forbidden.

options.text: ... there are the same number of inputs as outputs.
options.why: Equal counts are not required; the rule is about one output per input.

questions.solution_text:
A function pairs each input with exactly one output.
The first statement is correct.

questions.question_text: The relation $\{(1, 5),\ (3, k),\ (1, 5)\}$ is written with a repeated pair. For which value of $k$ is this relation a function?

options.text: Any value of $k$ works.
Only $k = 5$.
options.why: Outputs may differ between different inputs; the input $3$ may map to any value.

options.text: No value of $k$ works.
options.why: The pair $(1,5)$ is only repeated identically, so input $1$ still has the single output $5$.

options.text: Only $k \neq 5$.
options.why: There is no need to avoid $5$; input $3$ is separate from input $1$.

questions.solution_text:
The pair $(1, 5)$ is listed twice identically, so input $1$ still has just one output, $5$.
The input $3$ is different, so its output $k$ can be anything.
Any value of $k$ works.
